title: Rules
others: More games with Ton Up Pro

page.lockedBody: You can read the rules now. Playing it comes with Ton Up Pro.

x01.name: 501 and 301
x01.summary: Count down to exactly zero, finishing on a double.
how: Everyone starts on the same score: 501 for the standard game, 301 for a shorter one, 701 or 1001 for longer ones.
Take turns throwing three darts (a visit). The visit's total comes off your score.
scoring: Each dart scores its number, doubled in the outer ring and trebled in the inner ring. The outer bull is 25 and the bull is 50.
Going below zero, leaving 1, or reaching zero without a double is a bust: the visit scores nothing and your turn ends.
win: Finish on exactly zero with a double or the bull. Matches are played in legs, and sometimes sets of legs.
variants: Double in: scoring starts only once you hit a double.
Master out: finish on a double or a treble. Straight out: finish on anything.

dido201.name: 201 Double In, Double Out
dido201.summary: A short X01 that needs a double to start and a double to finish.
how: Start on 201. Nothing counts until you hit a double; from then on, count down as in 501.
scoring: As in 501, with busts below zero, on 1, or reaching zero without a double.
win: Check out on a double. It's a quick way to sharpen doubles at both ends of a leg.

gotcha.name: Gotcha
gotcha.summary: Race up to an exact target, and knock opponents back to zero.
how: Everyone starts on zero and adds each dart, aiming for an exact target, often 301.
scoring: If your total lands exactly on an opponent's score, their score goes back to zero.
Going over the target is a bust: the visit doesn't count.
win: First to hit the target exactly wins.

fives.name: Fifty-One by Fives
fives.summary: Only visits that divide by five count.
how: Throw a visit. If its total divides by 5, you bank the total divided by 5 points; otherwise nothing.
scoring: A dart that misses the board scores nothing for the whole visit. Going past 51 is a bust.
win: First to exactly 51 wins.
variants: Play to 61, 71 or 101 for a longer game.

cricket.name: Cricket
cricket.summary: Close 20 down to 15 and the bull, and score on the numbers you own.
how: The numbers in play are 20, 19, 18, 17, 16, 15 and the bull.
Each hit is a mark: a single is one, a double two, a treble three. The outer bull is one mark and the bull two.
Three marks close a number for you.
scoring: Once you've closed a number, extra marks on it score its value (25 for the bull) as long as an opponent still has it open.
When everyone has closed a number, it's dead and scores no more.
win: Close everything with as many points as anyone, or more. With a round limit, the most points after the last round wins.
variants: Cut-Throat, No-Score, Tactics, Random and Mickey Mouse Cricket change the numbers or the scoring.

cutThroat.name: Cut-Throat Cricket
cutThroat.summary: Cricket where your extra marks give points to everyone else.
how: Play as Cricket: close 20 to 15 and the bull with three marks each.
scoring: Extra marks on a number you've closed add its value to every opponent who still has it open.
win: Close everything with the lowest points (or level with the lowest).

noScore.name: No-Score Cricket
noScore.summary: A pure race to close all seven numbers.
how: Close 20 to 15 and the bull with three marks each. Extra marks do nothing.
scoring: No points are scored.
win: First to close everything wins. A good first game for beginners.

tactics.name: Tactics
tactics.summary: Cricket with 10 to 20 and the bull.
how: Play as Cricket, with every number from 10 to 20 and the bull in play.
scoring: As Cricket: extra marks score while an opponent has the number open.
win: Close everything with as many points as anyone, or more. Longer than Cricket, and it rewards treble accuracy.

randomCricket.name: Random Cricket
randomCricket.summary: Cricket on six numbers drawn at random, plus the bull.
how: Six numbers are drawn at the start and play as Cricket's 20 to 15.
scoring: As Cricket.
win: As Cricket.
variants: Hide the numbers until someone hits one.

mickeyMouse.name: Mickey Mouse
mickeyMouse.summary: Cricket with more numbers, plus any double and any treble.
how: A common version uses 20 down to 12, then any double, any treble, and the bull.
Rules differ by region, so Ton Up offers presets.
scoring: As Cricket: close each target with three marks, then score on it while it's open for someone else.
win: As Cricket.

killerCricket.name: Killer Cricket
killerCricket.summary: Close your own number, then take lives off everyone else's.
how: Everyone has a number. Close yours with three marks to start attacking.
scoring: Once you've closed yours, marks on an opponent's number take their lives.
win: Last player with lives left wins.

clock.name: Around the Clock
clock.summary: Hit 1 to 20 in order, then the bull.
how: Start on 1. Any hit on your number moves you on to the next.
scoring: Three darts a visit. You can move on more than once in a visit.
win: First to finish wins. On your own, try to finish in as few darts as you can.
variants: Skip ahead: a double moves you on two numbers and a treble three.
Leave the bull out and finish on 20.

nineLives.name: Nine Lives
nineLives.summary: Around the Clock where a blank visit costs a life.
how: Work from 1 to 20 as in Around the Clock.
scoring: A visit that misses your number with all three darts costs a life. Despite the name, you usually start with three.
win: Finish first, or be the last player with lives left.

hareHounds.name: Hare and Hounds
how: The hare starts on 20, and the hound a few numbers behind, often 5. Both go round the board clockwise, hitting each number to move on.
scoring: Each hit on your current number moves you one number on.
win: The hound wins by catching the hare; the hare wins by getting all the way round.
variants: The head start sets the handicap.

shanghai.name: Shanghai
shanghai.summary: One number a round, and a single, double and treble wins outright.
how: Round 1 is the 1s, round 2 the 2s, and so on, for 7 or 20 rounds.
scoring: Only the round's number scores: its value, doubled or trebled by the ring.
win: A single, double and treble of the round's number in one visit is a Shanghai, and wins at once.
Otherwise the highest total after the last round wins. Totals can tie.

halveIt.name: Halve-It
halveIt.summary: One visit per target, and a blank visit halves your total.
how: Work through a list of targets, one visit each, for example 20, 19, any double, 18, any treble, 17, then the bull.
scoring: Hits add their value. Missing the target with all three darts halves your total, rounded up.
win: The highest total at the end wins.
variants: Use your own list of targets.

bermuda.name: Bermuda Triangle
bermuda.summary: A Halve-It with a set run of targets.
how: Like Halve-It, but the targets are a fixed sequence that mixes numbers, rings and the bull.
scoring: Hits add their value; a blank visit halves your total.
win: The highest total at the end wins. Some sets call it Double Down.

countUp.name: Count Up
countUp.summary: A set number of visits, and everything counts.
how: Throw a fixed number of visits, often 8, and add up every dart.
scoring: Every dart scores its full value.
win: The highest total wins. On your own, it's the Count Up drill.

killer.name: Killer
killer.summary: Hit your own double to become a Killer, then take everyone's lives.
how: Everyone gets a number. Ton Up draws them at the start; at the board, each player throws a dart with their weaker hand.
Hit the double of your own number to become a Killer.
scoring: A Killer who hits an opponent's double takes one of their lives.
A Killer who hits their own double loses a life.
win: Run out of lives and you're out. The last player standing wins.
variants: More lives for a longer game.
No penalty for hitting your own double.

blindKiller.name: Blind Killer
blindKiller.summary: Killer where nobody knows who has which number.
how: Numbers are dealt in secret. Play as Killer.
scoring: Doubles on numbers nobody has do nothing, so you work out who's who as you go.
win: Last player standing wins.

scam.name: Scam
scam.summary: One player blocks numbers while the other scores on them.
how: One player is the stopper, closing numbers by hitting them. The other is the scorer, scoring on numbers that are still open. Then you swap.
scoring: The scorer adds the value of open numbers they hit.
win: The higher score as scorer wins. Rules vary from place to place.

baseball.name: Baseball
how: Inning 1 targets the 1s, inning 2 the 2s, through 9.
scoring: A single scores one run, a double two, a treble three. A perfect game is 81.
win: The most runs after nine innings wins. Ties go to extra innings.
variants: Settle a tie on the bull.

bullseyeBaseball.name: Bullseye Baseball
bullseyeBaseball.summary: Baseball where you need the bull before runs count.
how: Play as Baseball, but you must hit a bull in each inning before your runs count.
scoring: As Baseball.
win: The most runs after nine innings wins.
variants: A limit of six runs an inning.

golf.name: Golf
golf.summary: Nine or eighteen holes, fewest strokes wins.
how: Hole 1 targets the 1s, hole 2 the 2s, and so on. You can stop after any dart and keep it.
scoring: A common card: treble 1 stroke, double 2, single 3, a miss 5. Cards vary.
win: The lowest total wins.
variants: Par per hole, or just the front or back nine.

football.name: Football
football.summary: Win the ball on the bull, then score goals on doubles.
how: Hit the bull to win possession. While you have it, each double is a goal.
scoring: A visit with no goal loses possession.
win: First to 10 goals wins, or 5 for a short game.

ticTacToe.name: Tic-Tac-Toe
ticTacToe.summary: Claim squares on a 3×3 grid of targets.
how: Nine targets are laid out as a grid, with the bull in the centre. Hitting a target claims its square.
scoring: A claimed square is yours for the game.
win: Three in a row wins.
variants: Doubles or trebles only, or a random grid.

checkouts.title: Checkouts
checkouts.intro: The route to finish each score with three darts, double out. The bull counts as a double.

board.title: Board setup
board.heightValue: 1.73 m (5 ft 8 in) from the floor
board.ocheValue: 2.37 m (7 ft 9¼ in) from the face of the board
board.diagonalValue: 2.93 m (9 ft 7⅜ in) from the bull to the throw line
board.softValue: The throw line is usually 2.44 m (8 ft) from the board.
board.orientation: Hang the board with the 20 at the top, in the dark segment. Clockwise from the top: {order}.
board.rings: From the centre: the bull (50), the outer bull (25), the inner singles, the treble ring, the outer singles, and the double ring.
board.a11y: A dartboard with the 20 at the top

terms.def: The throw line. Your toes stay behind it.
One game of 501 or another X01, from the start score to zero.
A group of legs; win enough legs to win the set.
In X01, going below zero, leaving 1 or reaching zero without a double. The visit counts for nothing.
The darts that finish a leg, ending on a double.
180, the most three darts can score: three treble 20s.
A segment of the board, such as the treble 20 bed.
A single, double and treble of the same number in one visit.
A score with no three-dart finish: 159, 162, 163, 165, 166, 168 and 169.
Points scored per three darts thrown, the usual measure of a player's level.
Cricket's measure: marks scored per three darts.
